summary: The request-tree model and acquisition, captured-read and login rows are concrete. The biggest gap is the undefined constructors of the shared SDK error types (FetchError, HttpError, LoginError), and the acquisition row omits ADR 0029's digest request.

questions.text: What are the constructors of the guest-visible error types FetchError, HttpError, LoginError and the guest SecretError?
questions.reason: Every plugin, codec and CLI mapping (plugin.read-failed, tool.failed) pattern-matches on these. ADR 0014 requires FetchError to keep truncation 'distinct ... from a missing ID or corrupt/missing blob', and 0016's host SecretError has only SecretNotFound, but no ADR defines the variants.

questions.text: ADR 0009 fixes one AcquisitionRequests sum with no digest algebra, while ADR 0029 adds digestText as an Acquisition request interpreted by ContentDigest.
questions.reason: The row type, the ReadsEvidence injection depth and the generated dispatcher all change. ADR 0009 says 'Every source connector uses this one acquisition row' (Http :+: BlobAcquisition :+: Secrets :+: Waiting :+: FileRead :+: EvidenceRead), and ADR 0029 has 'digestText :: [Text] -> Acquisition payload [Text]'.

questions.text: How are host-side rejections reported for requests without an error channel, such as PutSecret with an invalid name or WaitSeconds with a negative duration?
questions.reason: The answer is either an invocation abort or typed results that change the wire contracts. ADR 0009 says 'Secret storage failures ... remain invocation failures' and requires host name validation and nonnegative waits, but PutSecret and WaitSeconds return ().

questions.text: What exactly does ListFiles return: files only or directories too, hidden or special files, symlink handling, ordering and missing-directory behaviour?
questions.reason: The folder connector's evidence IDs and removal detection come straight from this list, and followed symlinks can loop. ADR 0009 states only that paths are relative and that 'Enumeration failure is a typed error, never an empty directory'.

questions.text: What happens when an HTTP response (or request) body is not valid UTF-8, given that HttpResponse.body is Text?
questions.reason: The options are a typed HttpError, lossy decoding or an invocation failure, and each is a different plugin-visible contract. ADR 0009 says only 'Native HTTP handles TLS and UTF-8 transport'.

questions.text: How can a KB tool compare evidence with accepted facts when its Calls row has no snapshot reads?
questions.reason: This decides the tool broker row and whether tool invocation selects a validated root. ADR 0009 gives tools 'captured reads, model judgements and agentic model turns' only, but ADR 0014 says 'KB helpers can ... compare them with accepted facts'.

questions.text: Does SendHttp follow redirects, and if so does it strip credentials when crossing origins?
questions.reason: Silently forwarding an Authorization header to another host is a secret-boundary failure. ADR 0029 says 'Redirects use native HTTP handling without forwarding credentials to unrelated origins', but only for blob downloads.

questions.text: Do sink methods share the single FileWrite row, or can each sink declare HTTP, Git and Secrets requests, and how is that checked?
questions.reason: This affects registration inspection, generated adapters and the delivery handler set. ADR 0009's table allows 'filesystem/Git/HTTP/Secrets as declared' and ADR 0016 requires sinks to use the KB's secret store, but the only defined row is 'type SinkCalls = FileWrite'.
